title: Jab, Jab, Jab, Right Hook
author: Gary Vaynerchuk
blurb: Gary Vaynerchuk argues that social media is a boxing match for attention. Jabs are the small, generous pieces of content that entertain, inform or delight your audience without asking for anything. The right hook is the moment you finally ask: buy, sign up, visit. Most brands throw right hooks nonstop and wonder why nobody responds. The book's second big argument is that context matters as much as content. Each platform has its own culture, format and etiquette, so a story must be shaped natively for Facebook, Twitter, Pinterest, Instagram, Tumblr and whatever comes next. Through annotated critiques of real brand posts, he shows what works and what flops. The takeaway is practical: give consistently, tell stories that fit the medium, make your ask clear and easy, and keep adapting as platforms change.

lessons.t: Jab, Jab, Jab, Then the Right Hook
lessons.b: Win attention by giving value repeatedly before you ever ask your audience for anything.

lessons.t: Content Is King, Context Is God
lessons.b: The same message succeeds or fails depending on whether it fits the culture and format of the platform it appears on.
